extracted.subtask_description: A ten-month, mentor-guided romance writing program that takes unpublished writers from story idea to first draft through weekly partner-circle meetings, lessons, assignments, and one-on-one guidance; also describes eligibility and expectations for Guides. Includes curriculum, time/attendance requirements, selection, scholarships, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two basic elements of a romance novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that the two basic elements comprise every romance novel: a central love story and an emotionally satisfying and optimistic ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main plot centers around individuals falling in love and struggling to make the relationship work. A writer can include as many subplots as they want as long as the love story is the main focus of the novel. In a romance, the lovers who risk and struggle for each other and their relationship are rewarded with emotional justice and unconditional love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant eligibility (publication/contract status & readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to writers unpublished in novel- or novella-length romance fiction in a commercial market and not under contract or with an active pre-sale; prepared to meet participation requirements, writing commitment, and assignment due dates; agree to abide by the RWA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-members may participate but are encouraged to join RWA for the lower rate. Applicants should carefully consider availability and readiness before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant weekly time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must commit to devoting approximately eight hours (or more) per week to the entire ten-month program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time includes completing self-study assignments, participating in weekly Partner Circle meetings, meeting one-on-one with Guides, writing the manuscript, and critiquing peers’ work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant minimum attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants meet minimum attendance requirements (75%, or at least three live, online Partner Circle meetings per month) to remain in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are expected to complete assignments as outlined in the syllabus in order to remain in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of assignments / syllabus compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must complete assignments as outlined in the syllabus and engage with provided materials (articles, audios, videos, checklists, forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-study assignments prepare participants for Partner Circle discussions; weekly pre-work is expected before meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Participants are required to receive critiques on their manuscripts and to critique the work of other Participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner Circles will critique each other’s work; participants must give and receive useful criticism, treating partners with compassion and respect to enhance their craft and meet reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner Circles structure and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner Circles consist of six to eight program Participants plus two published author Guides who stay together throughout the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each week complete assignments before meeting; use circles for discussion, critique, accountability, and networking. Circles offer potential lasting relationships and writing partnerships. Guides facilitate and keep circles focused on proprietary content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant communications & support expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will communicate issues or concerns to their Guide or Participant Liaison immediately; a Participant Liaison keeps in touch to help address challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants expected to remain engaged and active; the Liaison helps ensure participants get the most from the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program outcome: draft completion and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: The program aims to guide participants through the craft to complete a first draft of a novel and provide structure for future books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants gain access to experienced authors, study materials, networking, and upon completion receive a Certificate of Completion; encouraged to enroll in a separate editing program afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants who meet qualifications are chosen on a first-come, first-served basis, contingent on the number of Guides available; a wait-list is established for early program availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment opens and closes on specified dates; capacity depends on Guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarship applicants must meet all Program criteria, attest to financial need, and complete the Scholarship Application Form; scholarships offered based on funds available as determined by the RWA Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representatives from the RWA Board, Diversity Advisory Committee, and Pen to Paper Committee select recipients. Scholarship applicants do not need to be RWA members. Recipients are expected to complete the entire program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds will be granted only if requested within the first seven (7) days of the program, minus a cancellation fee of $100. Refunds after seven (7) days may be processed case-by-case with documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must prove inability to attend due to circumstances beyond control (serious illness or death of registrant or immediate family member).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-deferrable enrollment / timeline adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment in this program is non-deferrable: Participants must begin and complete their program during the specified dates of their accepted enrollment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider availability and readiness; specific program timeline and dates are provided and must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course 1 — Creating Character-Driven Romances (learning objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Course 1 lessons: Knowing Your Reader and Subgenre; Articulating the Story Idea; Writing Interesting Characters in a Diverse World; Tapping into Characters’ Emotional Wounds; Analyzing Characters’ Goals, Motivation, and Conflict; Using Backstory to Fuel Conflict; Determining Story Structure for Your Genre and Subgenre; Using a Beat Sheet to Plot your Story as a Pantser or a Plotter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course focuses on character-driven craft foundation and gives specific lesson topics to prepare participants to build a novel's emotional and structural core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course 2 — Writing the First Draft (learning objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Course 2 lessons: Choosing Your Point of View; Twisting Tropes; Scene Goals, Settings, Hooks, Openings and Endings; Writing Descriptions that Suit the Setting, Mood, and Action; Writing Naturally Sounding Dialogue; Writing Exposition that Engages the Reader; Pacing Your Scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course centers on drafting techniques and scene-level craft to move from idea to an effective first draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course 3 — Writing Sexual Tension and the HEA (learning objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Course 3 lessons: Increase Scene Conflict; Relating Characters’ Emotional Wounds to the All-Is-Lost Moment; Writing Sexual Tension, Part 1; Writing Sexual Tension, Part 2; Writing the Grand Gesture and Happily Ever After; Determining Theme in Your Novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on climax, resolution (HEA), handling sexual tension, thematic development, and raising stakes/conflict toward satisfying endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides must be RWA members in good standing who are indie or traditionally published authors, RWA Associate Members with mentoring experience, or have experience mentoring other writers; prepared to discuss aspects of writing from idea generation through drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides should have previous facilitation/trainer/educator experience, reliable internet, reasonable computer fluency, and commit to being on camera for Circle meetings. Preference given to Guides with mentoring/learning facilitation experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide time commitment and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides are prepared to commit to completing the entire six-month course with an estimated time commitment of eight hours required each week (Guides must commit to a minimum time commitment of 6-8 hours each week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides must attend onboarding, review lesson materials and assignments weekly, conduct and lead weekly partner circle meetings, and participate in program events and workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide responsibilities in facilitation & critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides facilitate discussion in Partner Circle meetings, keep the Circle focused on proprietary content, use the syllabus and lesson materials to lead skill-set development, guide participants through activities, and lead the critiquing process based on skills developed in that Lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage progress and participation, reach out to participants who miss meetings, provide positive reinforcement, monitor progress and address issues, and communicate regularly with partner Guides and Guide Liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide one-on-one meeting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Program description notes Guides will facilitate one-on-one meetings: the program features six one-on-one meetings with each writer, and Guides are to facilitate multiple individual sessions (page states two progress sessions plus entrance and exit sessions resulting in a total of five one-hour individual discussions with each of their assigned Participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides are expected to hold these individual discussions (totaling multiple hours per participant) to coach work progress and provide individualized feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide administrative & platform responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides must use RWA Zoom accounts for meetings; record Partner Circle meetings; offer guidance through Groups.io boards and Zoom; and moderate Groups.io Circle content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides should monitor posted content for issues/concerns and direct questions or issues to the Guide Liaison. Notify liaisons promptly of problems or lack of participation for resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation & continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of each course, Participants complete an evaluation to provide immediate feedback that facilitates continuous improvement in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback is analyzed to identify continuous improvement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant behavioral/legal agreement & IP release
rubrics_metrics.description: By participating, you agree to release, waive, and discharge RWA (including directors, employees, agents) from liability from claims relating to participation, including misappropriation or misuse of any intellectual property or breached expectations of confidentiality regarding submitted works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should be aware of this legal release as a condition of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program logistics & timeline adherence (dates and onboarding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific program dates (application, enrollment, onboarding, course windows, guide interviews, and graduation) are set and participants/guides must follow the listed timeline (e.g., onboarding, Circle selection, course windows, graduation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should reference and adhere to the detailed timeline when applying and preparing to participate.
